items.followUp: State and prove Newton’s Second Law of Motion.

rubric.why: Checks the statement of the law.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force and is in its direction.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for the change in momentum.
rubric.how: Award for deriving the change in momentum from the initial and final momentum.

rubric.why: Checks the substitution of the momentum change and acceleration into the law.
rubric.how: Award for relating force to change in momentum per unit time and using the definition of acceleration.

rubric.why: Checks the final form of the law in SI units.

modelAnswer: Newton’s Second Law: The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the direction of that force.
For an object of mass m, changing velocity from u to v in time t, the change in momentum is Δp = mv − mu = m(v − u).
By Newton’s Second Law, F is proportional to Δp/t = m(v − u)/t.
Since a = (v − u)/t, F is proportional to ma.
In SI units the proportionality constant is 1; therefore, F = ma.
